body.meaning_en: to share, associate, be a partner
body.morphology: shirk is a verbal noun meaning the act of making a partner — in religion, associating another with God.
body.semantic_field: spans sharing, partnership, and holding a thing in common with another.
body.text_en: The root ش-ر-ك is plain partnership, two parties sharing in one thing as associates. Shirk is that idea turned against tawhid: setting up a partner alongside God, the one sin the creed of oneness exists to exclude.

derivatives.meaning_en: one who associates partners with God

lexicon.lane_en: شِرْكٌ ذ is an inf. n. of شَرِكَهُ , as mentioned in the first sentence of this art.: (Mgh, Msb:) or a subst. therefrom: (S:) and is syn. with , [signifying A sharing, participating or participation, partaking, or copartnership, and mentioned before as an inf.

body.meaning_en: to share, to associate as a partner
body.morphology: verbal noun of sharika, 'he shared / became a partner'
body.semantic_field: spans sharing, partnership, and association of one thing with another
body.text_en: The root ش-ر-ك is the ordinary word for sharing or taking a business partner. Shirk turns that neutral idea into the gravest error — assigning God a partner, sharing with something else the devotion owed to Him alone.
